name: BigONE
rootCause: BigONE suffered a supply chain attack in which adversaries deployed malicious binaries to the exchange's backend account-operation servers via compromised CI/CD or server management channels. The injected code silently modified the platform's account and risk-control logic to automatically approve withdrawal requests without legitimate authorization, bypassing normal security checks entirely without ever requiring the exchange's private keys. Attackers then drained funds across multiple chains — total losses reached approximately $27 million — of which roughly $4 million in ETH was the on-chain portion tracked on Ethereum. BigONE committed to covering all user losses from internal reserves. Attack Tx: 0x354e1d2b418fe303d66a1eaab66d15535616042c35305c2464983e5c92645da7 Analysis: Explained: The BigONE Hack (July 2025)

descriptions.text: Supply chain attack hit BigONE for $27 million when attackers compromised production servers and reprogrammed withdrawal systems to approve unauthorized drains. No private keys stolen - just someone who convinced the vault it was payday.

The injected code silently modified the platform's account and risk-control logic to automatically approve withdrawal requests without legitimate authorization, bypassing normal security checks entirely without ever requiring the exchange's private keys. According to monitoring by the SlowMist security team, cryptocurrency exchange BigONE has suffered a supply chain attack, with losses exceeding $27 million. The attacker breached the production network and altered the operating logic of servers related to account management and risk control, enabling unauthorized fund withdrawals. Notably, no private keys were leaked in this incident.

On July 16, 2025, BigONE crypto exchange lost $27 million in a supply-chain attack targeting back-end server logic. Hackers modified account control systems, enabling unauthorized withdrawals across multiple blockchains. User funds were not directly compromised, as private keys remained secure; BigONE publicly committed to fully reimburse all affected customers. Attackers exploited a supply-chain vulnerability to compromise BigONE's production servers, altering back-end account and risk control logic. This allowed them to bypass standard withdrawal checks and drain hot wallet balances without triggering private key or risk alerts.

The BigONE cryptocurrency exchange was hacked for more than $27 million, which the hacker quickly swapped for various other tokens. The attacker compromised one of the exchange's hot wallets after gaining access to the company's production network. BigONE stated they would fully cover the loss. Blockchain security researcher zachxbt responded to the hack by saying, "I do not feel bad for the team as this CEX processed a good bit of volume from pig butchering , romance, investment scams." Elsewhere he suggested that hacks of "sketchy offshore exchanges" would be a positive for the crypto industry, serving as a "natural cleanse".
